guidance.statement: Ind-Ra expects PJL's annual capex to be INR3-3.5 bn each year over FY26-FY27, with adjusted net leverage likely to fall below 2x and interest coverage to rise materially.
Ind-Ra expects a single-digit cement demand growth for PJL in FY26, led by housing and infrastructure demand in central India.
Plan to raise ₹300 Crores of long-term debt in Q2 FY26 to repay financial obligations, thereby proactively improving the overall debt maturity profile of the Company

Crisil Ratings expects consolidated EBITDA margin to improve to 8-9% in fiscal 2026 driven by pricing improvements and cost reductions in the cement division, particularly through green energy investments.

status_history.evidence: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin came in at 9.5%, above the 8-9% Crisil target.

guidance.statement: Crisil Ratings expects net debt to EBITDA ratio to gradually decline further over the medium term with an expected improvement in profitability amid no significant capital expenditure plans.

status_history.evidence: Net debt/EBITDA fell to 1.2x in FY26 from 2.4x in FY25; Crisil expects below 0.5x in FY27.

guidance.statement: Crisil Ratings expects the RMC segment profitability to remain strong with EBITDA of more than Rs 75-80 crore expected annually going forward.
Crisil Ratings expects consolidated EBITDA margin to sustain at more than 9% in fiscal 2027.
Crisil Ratings expects net debt to EBITDA ratio to improve further in fiscal 2027 to below 0.5x.
Crisil Ratings expects cement EBITDA per tonne to remain flattish in fiscal 2027.
HRJ margins are expected to sustain at more than 7.5% over the medium term.
RMC segment is expected to generate EBITDA margins of 7-8% going forward.

operating_notes.text: HRJ tiles division has 64 million m2 capacity across 11 units (including JVs) after Vijaywada modernisation and the 6.3 million m2 Panagarh greenfield plant.
Prism RMC operates 91 plants at 42 locations as on June 30, 2025.
Outsourced grinding capacity increased from 1.17 MTPA to 1.37 MTPA following RLJ Cement's 0.204 MTPA capacity enhancement at Mirzapur plant, Uttar Pradesh.
Prism Johnson declared preferred bidder for Piparhat Kubri limestone block, 203.815 hectares, 45.21 MT reserve, in Maihar district, Madhya Pradesh.
Prism Johnson declared preferred bidder for the Hinauti-2 limestone block, 17.534 hectares, 4.419 MT reserve, in Satna district, Madhya Pradesh.
RQBE turnover: FY23 ₹396 Cr, FY24 ₹316 Cr, FY25 ₹512 Cr; incorporated 14 August 2007, writes liability, health, property and motor insurance.
Cement EBITDA per tonne improved to INR708 in 1QFY26 from INR351 in FY25, aided by volume growth and cost savings.
Grinding capacity under supply arrangements rose to 1.37 mtpa as of mid-September 2025 from 1.08 mtpa at end-March 2025.
RMC EBITDA fell 39% yoy to INR0.17 billion in 1QFY26 after a 22% yoy volume decline due to completion of mega projects.

MP High Court order dated November 21, 2025 directed Sales Tax Authorities to issue Form C for HSD bought at concessional rate from July 2017 to March 2021; differential tax paid to be refunded or adjusted against future liability, amount n
Board approved sale of Windsor, 7th Floor, CST office premises to related party Windsor Realty Private Limited for ₹165.91 Cr, with sale deed to be executed by December 31, 2025.

GST inspection/search initiated at some offices and manufacturing unit in Maharashtra on January 30, 2026 under Section 67 of Maharashtra GST Act, 2017; company extending full co-operation and assistance.
During Q3FY26, the Company concluded the sale of its office premises located in Mumbai for a total consideration of ₹165.91 Cr.
On November 21, 2025, the Government of India notified the four new Labour Codes; the Company accounted for additional expense of ₹42.19 Cr towards gratuity and leave provisions.

During the previous year, the Company had received favourable orders from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal for assessment years 2006-2007 to 2010-2011, pertaining to additional grounds filed by the Company during assessment proceedings pri
Prism Cement has an installed capacity of 5.6 MTPA plus supply agreements with four grinding units for an aggregate 1.37 MTPA, and a dealer network of ~2,400 dealers.
H & R Johnson (India) has an installed tile capacity of approximately 64 million m² per annum across 11 plants (own and JV).
Prism RMC operates 87 ready-mix concrete plants across 41 cities and towns.
RQBE contributed 6.82% of consolidated turnover and 17.16% of consolidated net worth as on March 31, 2025.
Mr. Sanjaykumar Shivajee Roy has over 33 years of ready-mix concrete and construction experience, most recently as Chief Executive – Concrete Business at ACC Limited (Adani Group).
Penalty of ₹87,46,339 levied by the Jabalpur Central GST & Excise Commissioner for alleged wrong Cenvat credit availment during October-November 2013; company to appeal.

RQBE's independent fair market value was estimated at ₹551.84 Cr (₹10.32 per share) as on December 31, 2025 by Rarever Financial Advisors, against the ₹324 Cr agreed sale consideration for the 51% stake.
The divestment will terminate the joint venture with Australia's QBE Group in the general insurance business in India and the existing shareholders' agreement.
Mr. Sanjaykumar Shivajee Roy's remuneration as Executive Director & CEO (RMC) is capped at ₹3.57 Cr per financial year for a three-year term from March 2, 2026.
Income tax assessment order for AY2024-25 raised a ₹28,23,82,920 demand under Section 156 due to disallowance of certain expenses; the company is appealing and expects no material impact.
Shareholders approved the divestment of 51% in Raheja QBE General Insurance with 99.91% votes in favour; 91.27% of outstanding shares were polled.
Mr. Sanjaykumar Shivajee Roy was appointed Whole-time Director & CEO (RMC) with 99.97% votes in favour.

Mr. Sanjaykumar Shivajee Roy (DIN: 10174959), 57, appointed Executive Director & CEO (RMC) for three years from March 2, 2026; joined as CEO (RMC) – Designate on March 24, 2025; previously Chief Executive – Concrete Business at ACC Limited.

DGGI Jabalpur Unit inspected the Satna, Madhya Pradesh cement plant under Section 67(1) of the CGST Act on June 20, 2026, from 11:00 a.m. to 7:30 p.m., with no official communication on any alleged violation made yet.
RQBE divestment proceeds are subject to standard post-closing adjustments as set out in the Share Purchase Agreement.
ROCE increased to 9.4% in 2025-26 from 5.2% in 2024-25.
Free cash flow (pre-capex and investments) stood at ₹334 Crores compared to ₹529 Crores in 2024-25.
MPCB directed Kotak Mahindra Bank to forfeit a ₹10 lakh bank guarantee given as part of consent conditions for the Runwal Thane captive RMC plant, citing alleged non-compliance found in a site visit.

Samini Ceramics Limited (formerly Sentini Cermica Limited), incorporated January 11, 2002, makes ceramic tiles at a plant in Vijaywada, Andhra Pradesh; turnover was ₹78.40 Cr in FY24, ₹71.13 Cr in FY25 and ₹61.18 Cr in FY26.
Cement segment revenue was ₹902.53 Cr in Q1FY27, down 1.2% YoY from ₹913.55 Cr
HRJ segment revenue was ₹521.94 Cr in Q1FY27, down 2.1% YoY from ₹546.37 Cr
RMC segment revenue was ₹419.40 Cr in Q1FY27, up 26.8% YoY from ₹335.85 Cr
Cement capacity is 5.6 MTPA at Satna, Madhya Pradesh, plus supply agreements for 1.37 MTPA; sales concentrated in UP, MP and Bihar.
HRJ tiles capacity is 64 million m2 across 11 units (including JVs), with over 900 dealers and 22 large format experience centres.
Prism RMC operates 89 plants at 46 locations with 10.5 mn cubic metre capacity as on March 31, 2026.

timeline.summary: January 28, 2025: Prism Johnson received ₹128.1 Cr tax refund for AY 2007-08 to 2010-11
February 4, 2025: Prism Johnson approved sale of part of Pen tile plant to JSW Steel for ₹164.63 Cr, to be completed by February 8, 2025
February 6, 2025: Prism Johnson reported Q3FY25 consolidated revenue of ₹1,858.54 Cr (+7.5% YoY) and PAT of ₹46.03 Cr, aided by a ₹70.89 Cr tax credit and ₹82.33 Cr interest from an ITAT order.

February 25, 2025: Prism Johnson disclosed the resignation of Mr. Anil Suresh Kulkarni as Executive Director & CEO (RMC) and Director effective February 28, 2025, to pursue a career growth opportunity; MD Vijay Aggarwal will oversee RMC in the interim.
Arbitral Tribunal held GDCL liable for 80% of loss from silo collapse in interim award dated March 14, 2025.
On March 24, 2025, Prism Johnson appointed Sanjay Roy as CEO (RMC) and designated Gopal Bihani, Samir Jana and Anoop Sreekumar as Senior Management Personnel.

Shareholders via postal ballot approved re-appointment of Mr. Vijay Aggarwal (DIN: 00515412) as Managing Director and Mr. Sarat Kumar Chandak (DIN: 06406126) as Executive Director & CEO (HRJ) on March 29, 2025.

On April 2, 2025, Prism Johnson disclosed that tie-up partner RLJ Cement Limited's 0.36 MTPA Mirzapur capacity addition would be operational by June 30, 2025 instead of March 2025, taking RLJ's total capacity to 0.66 MTPA, while Prism's outsourced grinding capacity rises from 1.3 MTPA to 1.44 MTPA by June 2025.
Prism Johnson reported Q4FY25 results with revenue of ₹2,102 Cr, EBITDA of ₹188 Cr and PAT of ₹121 Cr, boosted by exceptional gains and tax refund interest.

On May 15, 2025, Prism Johnson appointed Mr. Sanjay Roy as Chief Executive Officer (RMC) and Key Managerial Personnel with effect from the same date, following a Nomination and Remuneration Committee recommendation.
On May 15, 2025, Prism Johnson presented Q4FY25 results showing revenue decline but EBITDA margin expansion driven by cost control in cement and improved mix in HRJ and RMC.

On May 28, 2025, India Ratings affirmed Prism Johnson's long-term issuer rating at IND A+/Positive and short-term ratings at IND A1+, cutting rated term loan to ₹737.6 Cr and withdrawing a ₹1.1 Cr unallocated limit.

On May 30, 2025, Prism Johnson terminated the 24 MW captive wind power project for its Satna cement plant and the related SSSHA and PCA with ReNew, citing material breach, and said it is entitled to liquidated damages and termination payment.
On June 25, 2025, Prism Johnson disclosed a ₹25.5 Cr investment in its subsidiary Raheja QBE General Insurance via a rights issue, with no change in shareholding.
AGM scheduled for August 7, 2025.

On July 23, 2025, Prism Johnson said RLJ Cement's Mirzapur capacity addition would be 0.208 MTPA against 0.36 MTPA planned, operational by September 30, 2025 instead of June 30, 2025, taking Prism's outsourced grinding capacity to 1.288 MTPA.
On August 7, 2025, Prism Johnson reported Q1FY26 results with 9.0% YoY revenue growth to ₹1,922 Cr but PAT turned negative at -₹5.56 Cr due to exceptional item reversal and tax changes.

On August 7, 2025, Prism Johnson's board approved a fundraise of up to ₹500 Cr through equity or equity-linked instruments, with the mode, price and terms to be decided by a Fund Raising Committee and shareholder approval to be sought by postal ballot.

On August 7, 2025, Prism Johnson's Q1FY26 investor presentation showed revenue up 7.8% YoY to ₹1,796 Cr, cement EBITDA per tonne at ₹708, and net debt at ₹771 Cr, with a plan to raise ₹300 Cr of long-term debt in Q2FY26.
Prism Johnson Ltd’s 33rd AGM held on August 7, 2025, via video conference from 4:30 PM to 6:09 PM (IST) with e-voting open from August 3–6, 2025.
On August 8, 2025, Prism Johnson subscribed 4,96,80,000 rights shares of Sentini Cermica at par for ₹49.68 Cr, raising its stake from 50% to 90% and making the ceramic tiles maker a subsidiary.
Shailesh Nagindas Dholakia disclosed 33rd AGM voting results on August 8, 2025, with all resolutions approved by shareholders.

On August 13, 2025, Prism Johnson's cement division signed a one-year supply agreement with Jabalpur Cement Industries for 0.09 MT of cement a year from its Jogidhana, Jabalpur plant, lifting grinding capacity via supply agreements to 1.38 MTPA by September 30, 2025.
On August 21, 2025, Prism Johnson issued a postal ballot notice seeking shareholder approval to raise up to ₹500 Cr via equity or convertible securities, mainly to repay debt.

On September 3, 2025, Prism Johnson disclosed that Crisil Ratings reaffirmed its ₹200 Cr commercial paper programme at Crisil A1+, citing net debt/EBITDA of 2.4x in FY25 and expected FY26 EBITDA margin of 8-9%.
On September 14, 2025, Prism Johnson reported that RLJ Cement completed a 0.204 MTPA capacity enhancement at its Mirzapur plant, increasing the company's outsourced grinding capacity to 1.37 MTPA.
On September 20, 2025, Prism Johnson said it was declared preferred bidder for the Piparhat Kubri limestone block in Madhya Pradesh, with a reserve of 45.21 million tonnes over 203.815 hectares.
On September 20, 2025, Prism Johnson shareholders approved a ₹500 Cr fundraise resolution through postal ballot

On September 22, 2025, Prism Johnson said shareholders passed the special resolution to raise up to ₹500 Cr via equity or equity-linked instruments, with 99.90% of valid votes in favour; the resolution was deemed passed on September 20, 2025.

On September 23, 2025, Prism Johnson said it was declared preferred bidder for the Hinauti-2 limestone block in Satna district, Madhya Pradesh, with an estimated reserve of 4.419 million tonnes over 17.534 hectares.

On September 30, 2025, Prism Johnson disclosed it subscribed to 2,39,09,000 rights shares of subsidiary Raheja QBE General Insurance for ₹38.25 Cr, allotted September 29, 2025, with its shareholding unchanged.
On October 23, 2025, India Ratings assigned IND A+/Positive to Prism Johnson's new ₹300 Cr bank loan facilities and affirmed existing ratings, including IND A1+ for commercial paper.
2025-10-30: Income Tax Department survey conducted; Q2FY25 board meeting postponed
2025-11-06: Prism Johnson said the Income Tax Department's Section 133A survey at its offices and plants concluded on November 5, 2025, with no material impact on operations.
Prism Johnson reported Q2FY26 results with revenue of ₹1,855 Cr, EBITDA of ₹186 Cr, and PAT of ₹1.59 Cr, marking a turnaround from a loss in the year-ago quarter.

On November 19, 2025, Prism Johnson disclosed that CESTAT rejected its service tax rectification appeal for a ₹22.57 Cr demand, with the company planning to file a statutory appeal and expecting no material financial impact.

On November 28, 2025, Prism Johnson disclosed that the Madhya Pradesh High Court, by order dated November 21, 2025, allowed its writ petition and directed Sales Tax Authorities to issue Form C for concessional-rate HSD purchases from July 2017 to March 2021, with the differential tax paid to be refunded or adjusted against future liability.

On December 18, 2025, Prism Johnson's board approved the sale of its Windsor, 7th Floor, CST office premises to related party Windsor Realty Private Limited for ₹165.91 Cr, with the sale deed to be executed by December 31, 2025.

On January 24, 2026, Prism Johnson disclosed that CESTAT had set aside a ₹34.1 Cr service tax demand including ₹26.4 Cr penalty (time-barred), but the Commissioner CGST & Central Excise, Jabalpur appealed to MP High Court, which admitted the appeal and set hearing for February 23, 2026.

On January 30, 2026, Prism Johnson disclosed that GST inspection/search proceedings were initiated at some of its offices and manufacturing units in Maharashtra under Section 67 of the Maharashtra GST Act, 2017.
Prism Johnson reported Q3FY26 results with PAT of ₹49.93 Cr and EBITDA of ₹139.69 Cr, driven by exceptional gain from office premises sale.
On February 27, 2026, Prism Johnson launched 'Prism Chakachak' Gypsum Plaster under its Prism Cement division, to be sold through its ~2,400-dealer network in Central India.
On March 2, 2026, Prism Johnson approved the sale of its 51% stake in Raheja QBE General Insurance to QBE Holdings (AAP) Pty Limited for ₹324 Cr, subject to shareholder and IRDAI approvals.

On March 2, 2026, Prism Johnson appointed Mr. Sanjaykumar Shivajee Roy, CEO (RMC) – Designate since March 24, 2025, as Additional Director and Whole-time Director designated Executive Director & CEO (RMC) for three years, subject to shareholder approval by postal ballot.

On March 2, 2026, Prism Johnson disclosed a ₹87,46,339 penalty order dated February 25, 2026 from the Jabalpur Central GST & Excise Commissioner for alleged wrong Cenvat credit availment in October-November 2013, which it intends to appeal.

On March 18, 2026, Prism Johnson issued a postal ballot notice seeking shareholder approval to sell its entire 51% stake in Raheja QBE General Insurance to QBE Holdings (AAP) Pty Limited for ₹324 Cr, against an independent fair value of ₹551.84 Cr, with proceeds mainly for debt repayment.

On March 30, 2026, Prism Johnson disclosed a ₹28.2 Cr income tax demand under Section 156 for AY2024-25 from the Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle 6(1), Mumbai, arising from disallowed expenses, which it will appeal.

On April 20, 2026, Prism Johnson reported that shareholders approved the divestment of its 51% stake in Raheja QBE General Insurance to QBE Holdings (AAP) Pty Limited for ₹324 Cr, with 99.91% votes in favour.

On April 20, 2026, Prism Johnson disclosed that shareholders approved the appointment of Mr. Sanjaykumar Shivajee Roy as Director and Whole-time Director designated Executive Director & CEO (RMC) for three years from March 2, 2026.
On April 24, 2026, Prism Johnson disclosed that arbitration proceedings with Doosan Power Systems India Pvt Ltd were concluded via settlement, with Doosan to pay ₹8.87 Cr by May 27, 2026.
Prism Johnson reported Q4FY26 results with flat revenue, improved EBITDA QoQ but PAT loss due to exceptional items and tax swings.
Prism Johnson's Board approved proposals to raise up to ₹1,250 Cr via NCDs and ₹500 Cr via equity-linked instruments, subject to shareholder approval.
Prism Johnson reported FY26 revenue of ₹7,404 Cr and reduced effective net debt to ₹646 Cr.
On June 20, 2026, Prism Johnson disclosed a DGGI GST inspection under Section 67(1) of the CGST Act at its Satna cement plant, concluded the same day with no stated material impact.
Prism Johnson completed the sale of its 51% stake in Raheja QBE General Insurance to QBE Holdings on 1 July 2026, ending the joint venture and terminating the shareholders' agreement.
Prism Johnson's Board approved the divestment of its 51% stake in Raheja QBE General Insurance to QBE Holdings on April 17, 2026, and received IRDAI approval on May 7, 2026.

2026-07-18: Prism Johnson disclosed that MPCB directed Kotak Mahindra Bank to forfeit a ₹10 lakh bank guarantee over alleged consent-condition breaches at its Runwal Thane captive RMC plant, with no material impact stated.
2026-07-31: Prism Johnson bought 52,78,500 shares of subsidiary Samini Ceramics from Sentini Buildtech LLP for ₹15.31 Cr, raising its stake from 90% to 98.5% on a fully diluted basis.
2026-08-06: India Ratings upgraded Prism Johnson's NCD and bank loan ratings to IND AA-/Positive from IND A+/Positive, affirmed the CP at IND A1+, and withdrew the fixed deposit rating.
Prism Johnson reported Q1FY27 results with revenue down 4.5% YoY but PAT turning positive to ₹112.7 Cr due to exceptional gain from property sale
Prism Johnson reported Q1FY27 results with PAT turning positive to ₹112.7 Cr due to exceptional gain from land sale and improved operational performance
Prism Johnson Ltd’s 34th AGM on August 7, 2026, approved standalone & consolidated financials for FY2026, appointed Vijay Aggarwal & Raakesh Jain as directors.
Shareholders at Prism Johnson Ltd’s 34th AGM (Aug 7, 2026) unanimously approved standalone & consolidated financials for FY2025-26 via e-voting (99.9987% in favor).
2026-08-18: Prism Johnson wins coal supply contracts worth ₹70.49 Cr per annum from Coal India subsidiaries
2026-08-27: Crisil reaffirmed Prism Johnson's ₹200 Cr commercial paper at A1+, citing FY26 net debt/EBITDA of 1.2x and ₹548 Cr liquidity.
Prism Johnson Ltd: Commissioner (Appeals) CGST, Bhopal set aside GST demand of Rs 22.7 Cr including penalty of Rs 11.35 Cr on September 3, 2026
On September 7, 2026, CESTAT New Delhi set aside the ₹11.53 Cr excise duty demand including ₹6.04 Cr penalty against Prism Johnson Ltd and its ex-employee.
Prism Johnson approved ₹40 Cr investment in KUS Renewable for a 49.5 MW captive wind power plant to supply power to its Satna cement plant.

Prism Johnson Ltd: Mr. Prabir Kumar Ray, Advisor-Business Development & Strategy, ceased to be Senior Management Personnel on completion of his term with effect from close of business on September 30, 2026.
